title: Error-controlled Progressive Retrieval of Scientific Data under Derivable Quantities of Interest
problem: Existing progressive compression approaches control precision only on primary data while leaving uncertainties in derived quantities of interest (QoIs). The challenge is extending error control from primary data to derived computations during progressive retrieval.
motivation: Unprecedented scientific data volumes overwhelm current storage and transmission systems, requiring efficient access mechanisms with precision guarantees.
method: The system mathematically tracks how errors from raw data flow through calculations to produce derived quantities (values computed from raw data). Rather than controlling accuracy only in the raw data, it identifies each source of error and how they combine during the derived calculations. It then designs a progressive data delivery system (sending data in incremental chunks) that keeps these combined errors within user-specified limits.
key_novelty: This framework guarantees that derived quantities calculated from progressively retrieved data stay within acceptable error bounds—the first to extend precision control from raw data to computed quantities.
contributions: Theoretical derivation for strictly controlling QoI errors during progressive retrieval applicable to any composited QoIs
Generic progressive retrieval framework design optimized through feasible progressive representation exploration
Comprehensive evaluation on five real-world datasets demonstrating 2.02× performance gain while maintaining QoI error bounds below 1E-5
